advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either remove/rename `test_self_contained_checkout_survives_shallow_source` or make `materialize_build_hook_package` actually consume the source repo's history so the shallow-source oracle is meaningful again.
evidence: tests/_build_provenance_fixture.py:34: `shutil.copy2(source_repo / "hatch_build.py", dest / "hatch_build.py")` — the only read of source_repo; no `git archive`/clone of the source
Removed helper docstring stated the shallow rationale: 'it fails outright when the source is a shallow or promisor (partial) clone whose historical objects are unavailable'

tests/unit/test_attestation_signing.py:446: `assert (shallow / ".git" / "shallow").exists(), "fixture source must actually be shallow"` then `materialize_build_hook_package(shallow, ...)` which never reads that shallow history
advisory.finding: The negative-control test `test_self_contained_checkout_survives_shallow_source` no longer tests shallow-source behavior. The old `_self_contained_checkout` ran `git archive HEAD` against the source repo (which fails on shallow/promisor clones), so the shallow clone was a meaningful stimulus. The new `materialize_build_hook_package` only does `shutil.copy2(source_repo / 'hatch_build.py', ...)` and never invokes git on `source_repo`, so the source being shallow is now irrelevant — the test passes regardless and its documented oracle is vacuous.
scenarios: A future regression that reintroduces reading source git history (e.g. `git archive`) would not be caught by this negative control.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact-text greps in test_artifact_probe_workflow.py with a behavior-oriented check (e.g. parse the YAML and assert the probe steps assert COMMIT equals the recorded checkout SHA), or drop them in favor of the CI run that actually executes the workflow.
evidence: The grepped tokens are the workflow's executable shell payload (the source under test), not a heading/canonical identifier/section — so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply; renaming the env var, reformatting the build command, or rewording the assertion message preserves behavior yet fails these tests.

The exact-commit provenance contract these tests describe is already exercised behaviorally when _artifact-probe.yml runs in CI (invoked by test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml), so the grep tests add no regression coverage of observable behavior.
advisory.finding: The two new tests in test_artifact_probe_workflow.py assert exact executable shell-command text (and the absence of old text) inside the workflow YAML rather than any observable behavior, making them change-detectors that break on a behavior-preserving refactor of the workflow.
scenarios: A future maintainer renames REBAR_EXPECTED_COMMIT or reformats the `python -m build` line without changing what the workflow does — both tests fail spuriously.
The workflow migrates from `${GITHUB_SHA::7}` phrasing entirely; the `not in` assertions become dead guards keyed to text that no longer exists.
